cues: Type zero, a general truth: if plus present simple, and present simple.
Type one, real or likely: if plus present simple, and will, can or may plus the base verb.
Type two, unreal now: if plus past simple, with were for every person, and would, could or might.
Type three, the impossible past: if plus past perfect, and would have plus the past participle.
Two rules hold for all four: never will or would in the if clause; and a comma only when the if clause comes first.
